exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Unsecured Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Unclassified or misclassified credential data directly results in unsecured credentials that can be discovered and exploited by attackers.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials from Password Stores
exploitedBy.relevance: Misclassified credential data may be stored in accessible locations similar to password stores, enabling credential theft.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials
exploitedBy.relevance: Improperly classified credential data can be gathered by adversaries as part of reconnaissance to obtain valid credentials.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Credentials In Files
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext credentials written to log files represent credentials stored in files that adversaries can directly read and exploit.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Log Enumeration
exploitedBy.relevance: Adversaries can enumerate logs to discover plaintext credentials that were inadvertently recorded during authentication events.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Keylogging
exploitedBy.relevance: Plaintext credential logging is conceptually similar to keylogging in that sensitive authentication input is captured and stored in an unprotected form.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Use Alternate Authentication Material
exploitedBy.relevance: Excessive retention of authentication artifacts such as tokens and session cookies allows adversaries to reuse them as alternate authentication material.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Web Session Cookie
exploitedBy.relevance: Retained web session cookies are a primary authentication artifact that attackers can steal and reuse to hijack sessions.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Steal or Forge Authentication Certificates
exploitedBy.relevance: Long-retained authentication certificates increase the window of opportunity for adversaries to steal or forge them for unauthorized access.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: OS Credential Dumping
exploitedBy.relevance: Audit records containing unmasked credentials can be accessed and dumped similarly to OS credential dumping techniques.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Transfer Data to Cloud Account
exploitedBy.relevance: Authentication data transferred across borders without controls mirrors the risk of unauthorized data exfiltration to external cloud accounts.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Automated Collection
exploitedBy.relevance: Bulk automated collection of authentication data for cross-border transfer increases the risk of large-scale credential exposure.

exploitedBy.label: MitreAttackTechnique
exploitedBy.name: Windows Credential Manager
exploitedBy.relevance: Cached authentication material retained in credential managers like Windows Credential Manager can be extracted by adversaries due to improper disposal.
